title: Unified Inference: Roadmap, PRD, Design Specs, Pricing & Release Notes (Q4 2026)
author: Avery Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design specs, roadmap themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference product line (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private) for Q4 2026. It is intended for cross-functional teams (product, engineering, go-to-market, sales, and customer success) to align on scope, success metrics, and launch commitments.

Key outcomes:
- Finalize v1.3 rollout for Redwood Optimize integration with dedicated pools.
- Publish pricing tiers and packaging for Dedicated and Private by 2026-12-15.
- Deliver rollout plan and runbooks for Canary -> Gradual -> GA with SLOs for latency and availability.

Goals and success metrics
-------------------------
Primary goals
- Make Unified Inference the single integration surface for customers across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Reduce mean token cost by 20% for targeted workloads using Optimize (batching + KV caching recommendations).
- Achieve 99.95% regional availability for Dedicated customers with SLA.

Success metrics (KPIs)
- API request latency (p95 generation latency) <= 350ms for short-form prompts (<= 128 tokens) on hosted tier.
- 20% reduction in per-token billable cost for 3 pilot customers within 90 days of enablement.
- Onboard 5 enterprise customers to Private deployments with audited KMS integration in Q1 2027.

Product requirements (PRD)
-------------------------
Scope (must-have)
1. Unified API surface: single REST/SDK contract for completion, chat, embeddings, and function/tool calling.
2. Model version pinning and rollout policy support (canary/gradual/automatic fallback).
3. Cost/latency controls: user-configurable batching window, concurrency limits, and per-route QoS.
4. Redwood Optimize v1.3 integration: automatic recommendations and one-click apply for batching/quantization profiles.
5. Observability: per-model and per-route dashboards showing token-level cost, latency percentiles, and cache hit rates.

Scope (nice-to-have)
- Prefetching suggestions for high-frequency prompt prefixes.
- Automated A/B model experiments at routing layer.

Non-functional requirements
- Security: must meet SOC2 controls already in place for Private deployments and support customer-managed KMS.
- Performance: runtime to support continuous batching without latencies above SLO for 95% of requests.
- Scalability: Dedicated pools must support linear scaling to 2x baseline traffic for each customer region with predictable throttles.

Constraints and assumptions
- We assume availability of the quantized model variants for the curated catalog by the model-onboarding team.
- Private deployments will use the same control plane version as Hosted but with customer VPC peering.

Design spec (high level)
-----------------------
Architecture overview
- Control plane: centralized service for model catalog, rollout rules, billing event emission, and telemetry aggregation.
- Data plane (serving runtime): highly optimized GPU runtime with KV cache, dynamic batching, and kernel selection.
- Routing layer: policy-driven router that can route by latency, cost, region, and customer tier; supports fallback chains to compatible model variants.

Key components and interfaces
- API Gateway: exposes REST/SDK endpoints; enforces per-tenant quotas and QoS.
- Router Service: accepts inference requests, applies policy, and routes to appropriate serving instances.
- Serving Pool: dedicated or multi-tenant runtime instances with autoscaling.
- Optimize Engine: recommendation engine that analyzes traces, cache hit rates, and token distributions and produces batching/quantization suggestions.
- Observability Pipeline: per-route tracing, token billing aggregation, and quality monitoring hooks.

Data flows (numbered)
1. Client -> API Gateway (auth + linting)
2. Gateway -> Router (apply route policy, select model variant)
3. Router -> Serving Pool (apply batching, check cache)
4. Serving Pool -> Runtime (generate response, update KV cache, emit metrics)
5. Metrics -> Observability Pipeline -> Optimize Engine (daily analysis)

Design trade-offs and rationale
- Centralized control plane vs. decentralized: centralized plane simplifies rollouts and metrics aggregation at the cost of cross-region control plane replication complexity. We accept replication cost to enable consistent rollouts.
- Aggressive batching reduces cost but increases tail latency; we default to conservative batching windows with per-route override to balance SLOs.

Roadmap and themes (Q4 2026 -> Q1 2027)
---------------------------------------
Themes by quarter
- Q4 2026 (current): GA for Unified API surface, Redwood Optimize v1.3 integration for Hosted & Dedicated, pricing & packaging finalized.
- Q1 2027: Private deployment KMS audit integrations, automated fallback chains, and 2 enterprise pilot migrations.
- Q2 2027: Model-level A/B experiments, advanced prefetching and caching heuristics, expanded regional footprint (APAC).

Milestones and dates
- 2026-11-30: Finalize API contract and SDK updates (v2.1).
- 2026-12-07: Release candidate for pricing & packaging (this doc).
- 2026-12-15: Publish public pricing page and partner-facing pricing decks.
- 2027-01-15: GA Redwood Optimize v1.3 for Dedicated.

Dependencies and owners
- Model onboarding: supply quantized model variants (owner: Research/Applied ML).
- Serving runtime: batching and KV cache improvements (owner: eng-serving-runtime).
- Observability: per-route dashboards and ingestion (owner: eng-platform).
- Legal & Finance: finalize contract language for Dedicated SLAs (owner: finance-and-legal).

Pricing and packaging notes
-------------------------
Guiding principles
- Transparent per-token pricing for Hosted API with usage tiers and committed discounts for Dedicated.
- Dedicated pricing: base monthly reservation + usage overage for burst.
- Private pricing: platform fee + integration/installation fee + optional support tiers.

Recommended tiers (summary table)
- Hosted: pay-as-you-go per-token; volume discounts at 10M and 100M token thresholds.
- Dedicated: Bronze (4 GPUs reserved), Silver (16 GPUs), Gold (64 GPUs) — each with baseline throughput guarantee, optional burst pool, and 12-month discount for annual commit.
- Private: enterprise evaluation license + per-node support; custom pricing for air-gapped deployments.

Example pricing (indicative)
- Hosted text-generation: $0.0008 / input token + $0.0012 / output token (baseline for standard models).
- Dedicated reservation: $X per GPU / month (sales to fill numeric placeholders per customer).
- Optimize add-on: additional $0.02 per 1k recommendations processed or bundled with enterprise for dedicated customers.

Discounting and partner rules
- Volume discounts applied automatically in billing when thresholds are met.
- Reseller/partner discounts require legal approval; standard partner program discount: 15%.

Packaging and GTM notes
- Self-serve sign-up for Hosted with free credits to encourage quick adoption.
- Dedicated sales-assisted onboarding with a solution engineer.
- Private deployments require pre-sales assessment and a professional services engagement.

Release notes (v1.3 candidate)
-----------------------------
Version: Unified Inference v1.3 (candidate)
Release date: 2026-12-07
Highlights
- Unified API: stable REST/SDK contract for chat, completions, embeddings and function calling.
- Redwood Optimize v1.3 integrated across Hosted and Dedicated for batching and quantization recommendations.
- Observability: per-route token cost and latency dashboards (beta).
- Rollouts: Canary/gradual rollouts with automatic fallback to compatible model variants.

Bug fixes
- Fixed race condition in KV cache eviction under high request fanout.
- Resolved a throttling miscalculation in Dedicated autoscaler when under burst.

Known issues & mitigations
- Some model variants still require manual quantization for low-memory GPUs; mitigation: clear customer communication and temporary routing to larger model variants.
- Cache warm-up can increase p99 latency for cold start; mitigation: pre-warming for top routes and prioritized warm-up during canary.

Launch plan and rollouts
1. Internal beta (2026-12-08 to 2026-12-18): select internal teams and 3 pilot customers to validate end-to-end flows.
2. Controlled preview (2026-12-19 to 2027-01-10): invite-only pilot for enterprise customers including Dedicated and Private pre-sales.
3. GA (target 2027-01-15): public documentation, pricing published, SDKs updated.

Operational runbooks and ownership
- Oncall rotation: eng-sre to own platform SRE for first 30 days post-GA.
- Support tiers: L1 handled by customer-success; L2 by eng-platform; L3 by eng-serving-runtime.
- Runbooks: see related pages for 'runbooks' and 'incident-review' links.

Open questions and decisions pending
- Finalize Dedicated GPU price per unit and published reservation tiers (action: finance and sales to confirm by 2026-12-10).
- Decide on Optimize add-on billing model (per-recommendation vs. bundled) — product & finance decision by 2026-12-12.

Appendix: API contract highlights
- Endpoint: POST /v2/generate
- Fields: model, input, max_tokens, temperature, route_tag, rollout_id
- Response: streaming chunked JSON with chunk.type and chunk.content fields and final metadata with tokens_consumed and model_version.

Contact and owners
- Document owner: Avery Chen (product)
- Release lead: Diego Ruiz (eng-platform)
- Runtime owner: Priya Nair (eng-serving-runtime)

If you have questions or require deeper technical design artifacts (sequence diagrams, proto definitions, or SDK diffs) see the related design documents in eng-serving-runtime and eng-platform.
